proposed.explanation: Society is addressed through Public obligation in the Code; not unique to Credo. Clients appear in both documents equally; not unique distinction. God/family relationships are personal domain, not professional stakeholder addressed in either document's obligation framework. The Code of Ethical Conduct structures obligations around Public, Client, Profession, and Fellow Architects. The Credo's Ethical Relationship principle adds 'industry partners' (contractors, suppliers, manufacturers) as an explicit stakeholder group not separately articulated in the Code. Sections 3-4 address contractor and supplier relationships within the Public/Client obligations framework, but the Credo elevates these to distinct stakeholder status. The Credo's Ethical Relationship principle uniquely emphasizes industry partners (contractors, suppliers, manufacturers) as a distinct stakeholder group beyond the Code's four obligation tiers.
